paragraphs.text: Paper-and-ink theme for DeepSeek Harness, with a living ASCII koi pond
# Dsh-Pond-Koi — a paper-and-ink theme for DeepSeek Harness

A theme bundle for the DSH Web GUI: warm paper, warm ink, hairline strokes,
near-square corners — an

d a living ASCII koi pond behind the whole
shell. The visual language is derived from a single-scree

n portfolio site; the
analysis that produced it lives in
cngtn-analysis.

Screenshots taken on the DeepSeek Harness desktop app **0.2.2-rc.1**, where the
theme follows the 0.

2.2 frame hooks (see the changelog for 1.5.2–1.5.4). The
older reference screenshots the palette was

measured against:
light / dark.
## What it is

Three layers, registered through the sanctioned third-party-theme extension point
(`ctx.theme.overri
deTokens`) plus one stylesheet and one canvas:
| Layer | What it does |
| **Tokens** (230+ pairs) | Paper and ink surfaces, hairline strokes, a tighter radius ladder, true
(non-squircle) corners, frosted menus instead of acrylic, and the koi vermilion as the only accent.
**No font family**: Settings → Appearance → Font decides, and the stock stacks apply when nothing is

chosen. |
| **Stylesheet** | The canvas layer and its paint order, the transparency chain that lets
the water show through the shell's frame, the frosted panels and Trajectory cards, and the site's u

nderline-only link treatment. |
| **Canvas** | The pond: koi with a 20-node spine, burst-and-coast t
ail beats, curiosity toward the pointer, food on click, startle on a fast swipe, depth dives, and an
ASCII raster that etches every fish into the same glyph grid as the interface. |
Disabling the plugin removes all three and the GUI returns to its stock design.
## Why it looks the way it does
The design system is four colours, one typeface and almost no decoration:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Everything else is derived: `color-mix` of ink over paper for strokes and muted
text, one typeface,

8px on cards and 6px on media, and a
single soft shadow reserved for the one elevated surface.

The one saturated colour is the koi. Its vermilion is step 3 of the pond's own
highlight ramp (`#cc3

e1c` on paper, `#e86038` on ink) and it becomes the accent,
the primary button and the business stat

e — but deliberately **not** the error
colour, because "error" and "brand" must never be confusable.
## The pond

The engine is a faithful port of the reference site's `koi-pond/` component,
split the same way:
| File | Ported from | Lines |

| `src/world.js` | `world.ts` | 440 |
| `src/shape.js` | `shape.ts` | 79 |
| `src/renderer.js` | `re

nderer.ts` | 672 |
| `src/engine.js` | `koi-pond.tsx` | 205 |

Nothing was simplified: the seven steering forces, the burst-and-coast tail
beats, the food-selectio

n hysteresis, the startle threshold, the depth model, the
five-point sub-sampled coverage test, the

body-anchored glyph hash, the
travelling sheen, the wake diffusion and both palettes are the origina

l's. A
pixel comparison of the darkest body colour against the reference agrees to
within one unit p

l comparison of the darkest body colour against the reference agrees to
within one unit per channel.
Three things did change, because a shell is not a landing page:

1. **Population.** The site seeds 3–6 adults plus two young koi on a full-screen
canvas. The theme a

sks for `budget: 0.55`, so a typical 1440×900 window gets
three fish — enough to read as a pond, few

enough to stay out of the way.
2. **Steering targets.** The site tags its own prose with `data-koi-

avoid`. A
theme cannot edit the shell's markup, so it names the shell's published hooks
instead (`[d

ata-slot="sidebar"]`, `[data-composer-card]`, …). Panels that
paint their own paper only steer the f

ish; the ones that do not also fade them
to a watermark, exactly as the site fades its prose.
3. **R

e-seeding on resize.** The site seeds once, because its canvas is always
correctly sized on the firs

t measurement. In a shell the canvas is inserted
before its stylesheet lands, so the first rect can

be the 300×150 default —
and the fish would be trapped in that corner forever. The world therefore
r
e-seeds whenever the box changes by more than a quarter.
### Seven varieties

The school is stocked the way a real pond is: mostly white-and-red, a few
patterned, and one or two
metallic or blue fish for depth.
| Variety | Look |

| kohaku | white, accent head and two or three saddles |
| sanke | kohaku plus small black spots |
|

tancho | white, a single accent disc on the crown |
| showa | black back, accent and white patches

|
| ogon | one metallic colour, paler along the belly |
| asagi | slate back, accent along the belly

|
| bekko | white, black spots only |

Each fish carries its own pigment, and the renderer derives a six-stop ramp from
it — shadowed at th

e flanks, lit across the back — so a gold koi is shaded by the
same logic as a red one instead of be
ing a recoloured copy.
## Layout

**The sidebar floats.** The frame is a three-column grid, and the sidebar keeps
its 280px track; the

cell gains 8px of padding so the card is drawn *inside* it
(264px wide) rather than shrinking the t

rack — the resize handle and the centre
column stay exactly where the shell put them. The card has a

14px radius on all
four corners, a hairline outline, the same frosted fill as the other panels, and

a **progressive shadow**: seven stacked layers whose blur grows geometrically
(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28,

44px) at low alpha, plus a 0.5px contact ring. One wide
shadow has a single edge and reads as a band

; the stack falls off the way a real
occluder does. Paper and ink get separate alphas, because a bla

ck shadow on a
dark page is nearly invisible.

The shadow needed the column to stop clipping: it had `overflow: hidden`, which
cut the shadow to a

12px band at the column edge. The column is now
[该节后续省略]
## What is deliberately not copied
| From the site | Why not |
| One screen, `overflow: hidden` | The shell is a multi-panel application; locking scroll would brea

k it |
| `px-[20vw]` gutters | The shell has a sidebar; gutters must follow the container, not the v

iewport |
| `pond / projects / gallery / blog` nav | The shell owns its navigation |
| Citation hove

r cards | There is no source data in the shell to cite |
| `defaultTheme="dark"` hard-coded | The us

er's Light/Dark preference is theirs to set |
| Playfair 14vw mobile menu | The shell has no full-sc

eference is theirs to set |
| Playfair 14vw mobile menu | The shell has no full-screen mobile menu |
The rule: **copy the visual language, not the information architecture.**
